provider_policy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

provider_policy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundary_decision.rationale: Accepted as `aggregate` on the subject axis. Campaign is a consistency and authorization boundary that mints and owns identities with no life outside it: plan releases, phases, waves, campaign-scoped assignments and variants, message and channel bindings, campaign metric definitions and campaign-specific evaluation assertions, while referencing party, project, activity, content, channel, budget, contract, event, observation, policy and audit masters by external identity. That owned-composition-plus-external-reference shape, together with the launch/pause/terminate authorization gate that must hold across declared scope, is the aggregate discriminator. Plain `entity` would understate the release and wave composition and the transactional authorization boundary; `event` would misread a durable governed root as its own transition log; `pattern` or `mixin` would deny it master identity; `registry` and `classifier` are contradicted by the model's own campaign-type and objective registries being declared Dimension-external. Record-plane axis, kept strictly orthogonal: a frozen registry value such as `standalone-mm` states only how the record sits in the model registry (standalone mega-model rather than profile, extension or sector overlay) and is never a subject-model entry kind, so this record can simultaneously be a standalone registry entry whose subject kind is `aggregate`. Residual challenges are recorded as holds rather than a reclassification: the STIX threat campaign and the Google Ads container are observed-behavior and platform projections that do not carry the mandate, release and authorization obligations of the governed root, and the model already declares that conflict.

decisions.concept: Campaign as the aggregate root rather than a projection of Project or Program
decisions.rationale: The declared discriminator holds: audience- or target-directed strategy, waves, message and channel intent, and campaign-scoped measurement are owned here, while ISO 21502-style delivery governance stays with Project/Program. The scope statement and the Project/Program boundary note keep the masters external, so the root earns its own identity rather than duplicating a delivery governance record.

decisions.concept: Entry kind axis separation between subject-model kind and registry record plane
decisions.rationale: The synthesizer must carry a visible statement that `aggregate` answers what the modeled subject is, while any registry plane value classifies only the record. Collapsing the two axes is the exact error that would corrupt downstream enum validation, so the distinction is recorded rather than assumed.

decisions.concept: Templated q02 and q03 provenance and validation questions across all 24 findings
decisions.disposition: rejected as researched interrogative content; publication hold
decisions.rationale: The kind histogram shows provenance 24 and validation 24, meaning two of three questions per finding are verbatim substitutions of the finding name into one sentence. Only q01 varies by kind, and even its declared kind (privacy, security, measurement) is not reflected in its text. This is a generated scaffold, not an interrogation of the subject, and cannot be promoted as researched material.

decisions.concept: Twenty-four artifacts sharing one media_or_form pair and one identity_strategy template
decisions.rationale: Every finding produces exactly one record artifact with the same two media forms and a name-substituted identity rule. A released plan, a suppression rule, a delivery observation and an attribution result have materially different form, mutability and integrity needs, so the artifact layer currently conveys no discriminating information and must be differentiated or partially collapsed.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity_strategy asserting campaign identity instead of artifact identity
decisions.rationale: The trailing clause 'name, date, timestamp and digest never identify the campaign alone' is a rule about the root, repeated 24 times inside artifact-level identity strategies. The artifact rule should constrain what identifies the artifact; the campaign-identity rule belongs once at the model level. The category slip must be corrected before the identity rules are treated as normative.

decisions.disposition: deferred pending vocabulary and escaping rule
decisions.rationale: The pattern {campaign-id}--{phase-or-wave-id-or-root}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id} references an artifact-kind vocabulary that appears nowhere in the model, and the '--' delimiter has no escaping or character-set constraint even though identity priority one admits arbitrary external master identifiers. Both gaps make serials non-deterministic in practice.

decisions.concept: Consent records and suppression lists placed inside campaign ownership
decisions.rationale: The eligibility finding names consent, suppression and membership as campaign-scoped, while the scope statement keeps party and membership masters external and access denies person-level segment membership. The defensible reading is that the campaign owns the versioned rule, the purpose binding and the effective interval, and never the consent or suppression record itself; the text must say so explicitly rather than leaving ownership implied.

decisions.concept: Retention of suppression and opt-out evidence beyond campaign disposition
decisions.disposition: deferred as an unresolved retention gap
decisions.rationale: The delete rule preserves lineage, decisions, observations and tombstones but is silent on the inverse case: an opt-out or suppression assertion normally must survive longer than the campaign that captured it, or the deletion of working copies silently re-enables contact. This directly contradicts the safeguard policy in effect and needs an explicit retention class.

decisions.concept: Access scopes expressed as bundle, layer, finding and artifact
decisions.disposition: rejected for person-level and protected data
decisions.rationale: Those four scopes describe the research record plane, not the subject graph. Person-level audience data, suppression lists, contact endpoints and cross-channel linkage must be scoped over campaign, release, wave, audience, segment and observation. Using documentation structure as the authorization scope is the same plane confusion the entry-kind rule forbids, and it would produce unenforceable access decisions.

decisions.concept: STIX 2.1 cited as support for mandate, authority, jurisdiction and access findings
decisions.disposition: narrowed to identity, lineage, object versioning and the adversarial profile
decisions.rationale: STIX models observed adversary campaigns, where no sponsor mandate, approved release or consented audience is available to the observer. Its use under sponsor/mandate/authority and under role-view/access/retention overstates support. It remains strong for campaign identity, aliases, object lineage and the explicitly declared threat-campaign profile.

decisions.concept: Missing neighbor boundary notes for Experiment or Trial, Consent or Permission, and Budget, Contract or Order
decisions.rationale: The phase and wave finding absorbs experiment, variant, hypothesis and assignment rule without any Experiment or Trial boundary note, risking silent capture of an experiment design master. Consent and Budget or Contract appear only as out-of-scope list items with no distinction paragraph, which is weaker than the treatment given to the five documented neighbors.

decisions.concept: Canonicalization by current lineage head versus the three-tier identity priority
decisions.disposition: flagged for an explicit resolution rule
decisions.rationale: Canonicalizing by 'authoritative source plus campaign identifier and current lineage head' can be read as making the head part of identity, while identity priority one makes the authoritative master identifier alone identifying. The head must be stated as a resolution pointer that changes without changing identity, or supersession will appear to re-identify the root.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist marking all sixteen dimensions covered
decisions.rationale: With a templated question and artifact layer, no approved relation rows, no live source verification and no independent review, 'covered' across every dimension over-claims. The synthesizer should carry the provider's dimension notes but publish the checklist as partial so downstream consumers do not read it as verified completeness.

decisions.concept: project-validate-retain-and-audit as a single function carrying nine source refs
decisions.rationale: Loss-aware projection, governed validation, retention and disposition, and audit evidence are four distinct operations with different authorities and different failure modes. Bundling them under one function with nearly the full source list makes source support untraceable, but the empty add_functions rule of single-provider mode defers the split rather than performing it here.

decisions.concept: Absent standards support for money and commitment, risk management, records retention and consent vocabulary
decisions.rationale: Budget, cost, currency and commitment cite only project-management guidance and one advertising platform; risk, hazard and control cite communication guidance and STIX; retention and disposition cite no records standard; consent and privacy rest on a tier-two Schema.org term. Candidate standards must be identified and verified live before these findings can claim source grounding.

deferred_research: Cross-sector adversarial review of the Campaign root by political communication, public-health, marketing, fundraising, advocacy, security and legal reviewers, since the current source base leans on two public-health bodies, one project-management standard, four W3C vocabularies and one advertising platform.

Identify and live-verify standards support for the four weakly grounded areas: money, cost and commitment representation (currency-code standard as a candidate), risk and control management, records retention and disposition, and consent or processing-purpose vocabulary. Each candidate must be resolved and version-pinned before it is cited.

Author the missing neighbor boundary notes for Experiment or Trial, Consent or Permission, and Budget, Contract or Order, and decide explicitly whether experiment design, randomization unit, assignment rule and variant belong to a separate Experiment aggregate rather than inside the campaign wave finding.

Resolve the canonicalization tension by stating whether the current lineage head is part of canonical identity or only a resolution pointer, and define what supersession, duplicate merge and campaign-successor do to the root identifier and to already-released artifacts.

Define a retention class for suppression, opt-out and withdrawal evidence that survives campaign closure and working-copy deletion, and reconcile it with data minimization, legal hold and the deny-by-default person-level access rule.

Re-scope access control over the subject graph (campaign, release, wave, audience, segment, assertion, observation) and specify how participant-self disclosure answers a membership question without minting a new membership assertion.

De-duplicate the three findings that each carry incident semantics (risk and compliance, lifecycle transition, plan release and recovery), decide which definition-only findings should be inline_only rather than producing a serial artifact, and split the overloaded project-validate-retain-and-audit function into projection, validation, retention and audit operations.

Decide whether a distinct honor-withdrawal, suppression-enforcement and adverse-effect-response function is required, since the current function set defines audiences and safeguards at plan time but has no runtime operation that enforces a withdrawal or halts delivery on a safety signal short of a full pause or terminate.

Attempt bounded supplemental Claude and Grok passes when either becomes available, admitting a result only if it is locally schema-valid and its sources and boundaries survive the same adjudication, so that the absence-of-external-review hold can eventually be lifted rather than permanently waived.
publication_holds: Live source and version verification hold: no source URL, version or date was resolved during this no-tools audit. SRC-006 cites ISO 21502 through a committee page for normative text that is paywalled and not readable at that URL; SRC-007 carries an access date but no version; SRC-008, SRC-010, SRC-011 and SRC-012 pin 2026 publication or API versions; SRC-013 pins RFC 3339 as updated by a later RFC. Every pin must be re-fetched, re-dated and re-pinned before promotion, and any unresolvable URL must drop the findings that depend on it to unsupported.

Absence-of-independent-review hold, owner-authorized: the repository owner waived Claude on 2026-09-06 after 1800, 900, 600 and 300 second attempts produced no result, and waived Grok as unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Codex is therefore the sole active provider, and this no-tools adversarial pass audits that same stream from local evidence only. It is not, and must never be described as, independent external second-provider review. The waiver, its authorization, and this limitation must appear in every publication artifact.

Relationship contract hold: frozen_context is empty and no approved relation rows were supplied, so the registry parent link to Project and the proposed party, activity, content, channel, budget, contract, event, observation, policy and audit links remain unadjudicated. Publish with no asserted relations and with the parent link shown as a pending hold rather than an implied edge.

Question and artifact template hold: q02 and q03 are template-identical across all 24 findings and every artifact reuses one media_or_form pair and one name-substituted identity strategy that mistakenly constrains campaign identity rather than artifact identity. The interrogative and artifact layers must be rewritten per finding, and the {artifact-kind} token plus delimiter escaping must be defined, before canonical promotion.

Protected-data and operational-guidance hold: access scopes are drawn from the record plane (bundle, layer, finding, artifact) rather than the subject graph, suppression and opt-out retention beyond campaign disposition is unspecified, and consent ownership is only implicitly external. Do not publish or operationalize targeting, suppression, consent or cross-channel linkage guidance from this draft, and do not treat its access rules as enforceable authorization.

Coverage and status hold: the provider checklist marks all sixteen dimensions covered while the model itself declares that no independent result was obtained and that sector profiles are missing. Publish as reviewable draft with the checklist downgraded to partial, pending cross-sector, political, public-health, marketing, fundraising, advocacy, security, privacy and legal review.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
